path.title: Reindeer Herders Cross Continents
path.summary: Permanent land allows Siberian reindeer herding, sled design, and cold-climate clothing techniques to spread gradually into Alaska by foot and caravan. Northern communities on both sides develop a shared seasonal round, exchanging breeding animals and knowledge each year.

branches.title: Rotating Lichen Pastures Sustain Herds
branches.summary: Communities formalize rotational grazing that lets lichen recover between seasons, improving herd health across the shared seasonal round. This follows because annual exchanges of herders and breeding animals spread observations about overgrazed ground and recovery times to both sides of Beringia.
branches.scene: At dawn, families move a scarlet-ribboned herd between stone markers while children record fresh lichen growth on birch-bark charts.
branches.causalLink: The shared seasonal round from 900 brought herders repeatedly to the same pastures, making lichen depletion visible and prompting agreed rotation schedules exchanged at annual meetings.

branches.title: Herders Map Interior River Routes
branches.summary: Reindeer sled teams extend seasonal travel inland, producing route maps of Alaskan rivers, passes, and shelter sites shared among northern communities. This exploration is possible because reliable herds, sled designs, and cold-climate clothing from the cross-Beringian exchange reduce the risks of long winter journeys.
branches.scene: A sled driver unrolls a hide map etched with rivers and wind shelters, tracing the next leg while reindeer steam in the low sun.
branches.causalLink: The established cross-continental seasonal round created dependable herds, staging pastures, and guide knowledge that could be extended from coastal Beringia into Alaska's interior.

branches.title: Antler Carving Schools Blend Motifs
branches.summary: Carvers in Beringian settlements combine Siberian and Alaskan animal motifs into a shared antler and ivory carving curriculum taught to apprentices. Regular caravan contact and intercommunity seasonal gatherings follow from the herder exchanges, giving artists repeated access to new tools, stories, and styles.
branches.scene: In a turf-roofed workshop, an apprentice finishes a reindeer whose antlers curl into a salmon, beside carvings traded from across the land bridge.
branches.causalLink: Annual herder caravans carrying breeding animals and sled equipment also carried portable carvings and carvers, allowing motifs and techniques to be taught during winter gatherings.
